fix: Minimal and conservative: feed a premise-challenge FAIL into failure-learning WITHOUT making it authoritative (do NOT add it to the ship floor — that would halt cycles on an advisory judgment gate and is a much larger behavior change). Route the FAIL through the existing recordFloorVerdictFailure seam (or a sibling that writes state.FailedAt / failedApproaches without the floor semantics) so the failure-adapter and Scout can see that THIS framing was refused, and surface the blocking reason in the dossier/summary rather than only in the workspace artifact. Red-first: fixture where premise-challenge returns VerdictFAIL -> assert (a) state.FailedAt records the refused framing with its reason, (b) the cycle still proceeds (no halt — this is explicitly NOT a stop-the-lane change), and (c) a subsequent Scout dispatch receives the refused framing in its failure context. Guard: authoritative-phase FAIL behavior byte-identical; premise-challenge PASS byte-identical; remediationDenied unchanged (still no re-roll). || ATTEMPT 1 BLOCKED BY REVIEW (branch fix/judgment-phase-learning, opus) — four things learned, all recorded so the next attempt starts ahead. (1) DO NOT derive the phase set as `remediationDenied[p] && !isAuthoritativePhase(p)`: remediationDenied has SIX members, and subtracting only the ship floor leaves {adversarial-review, premise-challenge, plan-review, RETRO, DEBUGGER}. failure_learning.go:337 ALREADY excludes PhaseRetro from failure-learning by an explicit guard, and calling recordFailedApproachState directly routes around it; worse, cyclerun_record.go:154/159/172 feed state.FailedAt into decideAfterRetro, so a retro's own quota blip would inflate the evidence for its own disposition in the same cycle. Use an EXPLICIT set, and pin teachesWithoutHalting(PhaseRetro)==false and (PhaseDebugger)==false. (2) THE 'DOES NOT HALT' CLAIM IS NOT ESTABLISHED by skipping persistFloorFailReasons. decision_branch.go:160-169 feeds state.FailedAt through entriesFromRecords -> failureadapter.Decide, and ActionBlockCode/ActionBlockOperatorAction return recoveryTarget(PhaseRetro, ..., PhaseEnd). Records persist to state.json and merge forward, so accumulated advisory refusals become indistinguishable from floor failures on a later cycle. This must be closed or justified before shipping — the adapter's exact thresholds were NOT determined. (3) MY CONSTRAINT COMMENT WAS FACTUALLY WRONG: persistFloorFailReasons sets a CycleState field ONLY for PhaseAudit (system_failure.go:66-82); for premise-challenge it writes a forensic JSON only, so the halt-arming mechanism I cited does not exist for these phases. The REAL halt vector is (2). (4) Records default to Classification 'cycle-mid-execution-fail' and Retrospected:true — the former is NOT in failureadapter's closed taxonomy (failureadapter.go:24-37, mirroring scripts/failure/failure-classifications.sh), and sameClassStreak keys the ADR-0072 non-progress counter off Classification, so repeated advisory refusals manufacture a same-class streak and inflate failure-dossier.json. Any fix should give these records their own honest classification and priority (P0 is wrong for a gate that by design cannot halt; failure_learning.go:325 hardcodes it with no caller parameter). ALSO REQUIRED: a test that drives recordAndBranch and asserts BOTH halves — the record lands AND the cycle proceeds; the attempt's unit tests left the wiring unpinned, so deleting the new branch entirely kept them green. And check whether resume.go:365 needs the same wiring (recordFloorVerdictFailure's lockstep note says a fix wired into one site leaves the other exposed). || RESEARCH RESOLVING THE BLOCK-2 HALT QUESTION (read directly, not inferred). (a) failureadapter.Decide's rules read ONLY these class keys: ByClass[InfraSystemic], ByClass[InfraTransient], ByClass[IntentRejected], plus distinctCyclesByClass(CodeAuditFail) and distinctCyclesByClass(CodeBuildFail). A record whose Classification is outside that set of five CANNOT trigger any BLOCK rule. The current default, 'cycle-mid-execution-fail', is already outside it. (b) EVERY blocking rule is gated on opts.Strict; in the fluent posture each appends a 'would-have-blocked: ...' awareness string instead of returning an Action — which is exactly what cycle-1530's RetroDecision showed live ('proceed: fluent mode ... would-have-blocked: BLOCK-CODE — 33 non-expired code-audit-fail entries'). (c) Evidence.NonExpiredCount is used ONLY to compose the PROCEED message (failureadapter.go:248); it is never a threshold. So the 'FailedAt -> Decide -> PhaseEnd' halt vector is NOT reachable for an out-of-taxonomy classification. TWO REAL SIDE EFFECTS THE REVIEW DID NOT NAME, both from appending to FailedAt at all: (1) tailInfraTransientStreak (failureadapter.go:309-320) walks the TAIL and BREAKS on any non-infra-transient class, so an advisory refusal appended mid-run would end an in-progress infra-transient streak and could suppress a RETRY-WITH-FALLBACK the streak would have produced. Note this is not a NEW class of interference — every non-infra failure record already breaks that streak — but it is a behavior change. (2) sameClassStreak (failure_dossier.go:117-129) takes the LAST record's Classification and counts backward while identical, so CONSECUTIVE advisory refusals would manufacture a same-class streak feeding the ADR-0072 non-progress numbers. => RECOMMENDED DESIGN, which sidesteps both: record ONLY the carryover todo, and do NOT append a FailedRecord to state.FailedAt. The carryover todo is the Scout-visible memory that cycle-1528 actually lost; the FailedAt record is what drags in the adapter and the dossier. That needs recordFailedApproachState split (or a flag on failureLearningRequest) so the todo half can be used without the record half — verify the split point before coding, and give the todo a priority below P0 (failure_learning.go:325 hardcodes P0 with no caller parameter).
notes: Filed per the 2+-occurrence class rule (3 occurrences: 1526 M2, 1527, 1528). Deliberately scoped AWAY from the tempting fix (make premise-challenge authoritative / halt on BLOCK): that would convert an advisory judgment gate into a lane-stopper and is not supported by the evidence here. The demonstrated harm is not 'a bad cycle ran' — 1528 may still produce something useful — it is that a CRITICAL, line-cited refutation evaporates from the system's memory the moment the phase ends, leaving Scout free to re-derive it. Verified by direct code read, not inference: grep over go/ shows NO reader of premise-challenge-report.md outside tests. HARM CONFIRMED BY PREDICTION (cycle-1528 build diff, inspected AFTER the prediction was recorded and BEFORE audit): the lane built EXACTLY the design its own premise-challenge refuted. engine.go +43 adds 'if apiErr := apiErrorLine(stderrBuf.String()); apiErr != "" { ... } else if summary := artifactTimeoutSummary(stderrBuf.String())' — reading the stderr buffer the challenge proved structurally never carries provider error text, with apiErrorTransientRe = `(?i)\b(?:429|529)\b|overloaded|rate[ _-]?limit|quota`. Note the literal 'quota' alternative: the challenge named this specific token as matching the exit-81 drift alarm (exhaustion_drift.go:39-41, emitted at driver_tmux_repl.go:869 just before the marker at :880), and the new code gives apiErrorLine PRECEDENCE over artifactTimeoutSummary (if / else-if), which is the exact displacement that regresses engine.go:551-561. It did NOT touch autorespond.go, the pane-matcher seam that actually sees the 529 text. Files: engine.go +43, engine_artifact_timeout_apierror_test.go +179, acs/cycle1528/predicates_test.go +124 — i.e. 303 lines of test pinning a classifier that cannot fire in production, which is precisely the '3/3 GREEN while the production defect is untouched' outcome the challenge predicted. Whether the adversarial auditor catches it downstream is a separate question; the point here is that a CRITICAL line-cited refutation produced zero mechanical effect on what got built. DOWNSTREAM GATE CAUGHT IT — SCOPE THIS ITEM CORRECTLY: cycle-1528's adversarial-review returned evolve-verdict {"phase":"adversarial-review","verdict":"FAIL"} on the same change, with a BETTER analysis than the premise-challenge: F1 HIGH (indirect prompt injection — the exit-81 stderr buffer is NOT purely bridge-authored; it carries stop-review reasons embedding pane text via 'matched %q' at fatalpane.go:111 and the agent-chosen workspace file listing at driver_common.go:363-390, so an agent naming a file '529-overloaded.txt' can steer the recorded cause into retroCtx['failure_error'] and thus into the retro agent's prompt, re-opening the channel artifactTimeoutSummary was built to close per engine.go:552-557) and F2 MEDIUM (the drift alarm's own 'quota' text outranking the timeout summary — the exact collision premise-challenge predicted). CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS ITEM: the harm is NOT 'a defect ships' — the gate stack held. The harm is (a) a full deep-tier build cycle spent on a design already refuted in writing, and (b) the refutation leaving no trace in state.FailedAt, so Scout may re-derive the identical framing next cycle. Scope the fix to failure-LEARNING only; do not argue for halting on premise-challenge BLOCK on the strength of this evidence, because the downstream gate demonstrably did its job. ACCURACY NOTE (corrected against cycle-1528's audit H2): premise-challenge's claim that every deps.Stderr write on the exit-81 path is bridge-authored is LITERALLY CORRECT and the auditor independently restated it — 'on the only exit-81 emitter every deps.Stderr write is bridge-authored (driver_tmux_repl.go:849-880); a genuine provider 429/529 line never reaches stderrBuf'. It was INCOMPLETE, not wrong: bridge-AUTHORED lines still embed UNTRUSTED CONTENT — agent-chosen workspace filenames (driver_tmux_repl.go:850-852 via driver_common.go:363-390) and pane text via 'matched %q' (fatalpane.go:111). So both gates were right about different halves: provider text never gets IN (classifier cannot fire as intended), while attacker-controlled text DOES (classifier fires on the wrong thing). Final disposition: audit FAILed the cycle with H1+H2 HIGH; the lane went to retro and never reached ship.
root_cause: Two independent gaps compound. (1) BRANCHING: cyclerun_record.go:117 gates failure recording on 'dr.resp.Verdict == VerdictFAIL && cr.o.isAuthoritativePhase(next)'. isAuthoritativePhase (final_verdict_floor.go:36-41) is 'phase == PhaseShip || slices.Contains(o.resolvedShipFloor(), phase)' — premise-challenge is not on the ship floor, so recordFloorVerdictFailure is never called: state.FailedAt is not set, the failure-adapter and Scout never see it, and recordFinalVerdict files the outcome into result.VerdictsNotAdopted. (2) CONSUMPTION: no Go code reads premise-challenge-report.md at all (grep over go/ excluding tests returns zero hits) — the verdict reaches the builder only as injected prompt context, i.e. an LLM decides whether to honor its own upstream gate. Note the asymmetry this creates: premise-challenge IS on remediationDenied (cyclerun_remediate.go:43-50, 'granting the builder a re-roll against an LLM-judgment verdict would be a gamed verdict') — too authoritative to re-roll, not authoritative enough to stop or to teach. The comment immediately above cyclerun_record.go:117 describes this exact disease for deterministic gates: 'the failure-adapter and Scout were blind to it and a self-defeating task (the skills-drift storm, cycles 836/838/841/843/849) re-derived the same doomed fix forever.'
summary: Live, 3 occurrences. Cycles 1527 AND 1528 (wave batch-20260819b) each emitted a well-formed machine-readable verdict — 'evolve-verdict: {"phase":"premise-challenge","verdict":"FAIL","schema_version":1}' — with prose 'FAIL (BLOCK) — the cycle must NOT proceed to build as framed'. BOTH lanes advanced to tdd and build regardless. Cycle-1526's auditor independently flagged the adjacent shape as M2 MEDIUM ('build dispatch treated the advisory premise-challenge BLOCK as fully discharged by item 3 alone'). Cycle-1528's challenge was not a style objection: it proved with enumerated line cites that the lane's planned apiErrorLine classifier reads a buffer (Engine.Launch's stderr on exit-81) that structurally NEVER contains provider error text, so the fix would pass its acceptance 3/3 GREEN while never firing in production — and the lane proceeded to build it anyway.
title: A premise-challenge FAIL (severity_max=CRITICAL, 'the cycle must NOT proceed as framed') neither halts the lane nor reaches failure-learning — the verdict is filed to VerdictsNotAdopted, state.FailedAt stays clean, and Scout is free to re-derive the identical doomed framing next cycle
